# SkinnedMeshRenderer

Draws a skinned mesh from a glTF file, driven by an Animation on the same object.

Availability: **PSX** no | **PSP** yes | **PS2** yes

The component or type needs the `skinning` feature (skeletal animation (psx uses segmented rigid models)). If it is missing: use sprite or vertex animation.

`mesh` is the glTF asset (its first skinned mesh); `material` is a `.mat.json`. The cooker splits a mesh whose triangles touch more bones than the profile draws at once into batches, so the artist does not have to.

## Members

| Member | PSX | PSP | PS2 | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Guid mesh` | no | yes | yes | The glTF asset. |
| `Guid material` | no | yes | yes | The material: texture, color, unlit, alpha test. |

## Limits

| Limit | PSX | PSP | PS2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bones per draw (0 = not batched) | 0 | 8 | 0 |
| Skinned joints per skeleton (0 = none) | 0 | 64 | 64 |

## Notes

- The component needs the `skinning` feature. A scene that uses it on a profile without the feature is refused by the cooker, naming the object.
- Vertices are stored in a compact 16-bit form for the PSP; the PC builds use floats. Both give the same game state.

## Example

```cpp
// Normally set in the editor. At run time, swap the material:
GameObject::Find("Hero")->GetComponent<SkinnedMeshRenderer>()->material = hurtMaterial;
```

See also: [API availability by profile](../api-availability.md), [API index](index.md).
